result:
**Round 267 (GATE264-S2) is a FAIL.** Every acceptance row in the task passes in the real browser at 1440×900 and 1280×720, but A's open STOP is a real Medium regression. The browser rows ran (`browserVerified` and `realVerified` are true), and B has not yet ruled on the STOP.

**The bug (C-R267-01, Medium):** while a mouse drag is held, a Ctrl+ArrowRight key event with AltGraph set and Alt not set now moves the insert marker from 7.500 to 101.352 (the clip end), with no "Editing does not work while dragging" message.
- I compared the same script against a server built from the published code (7ba7cd2, run on :5174). There the same key is blocked with that message and the marker stays put. Results at both window sizes are in `c-round-267/gesture-head.json` and `gesture-diff.json`.
- The cause is the task's own instruction: §2.1.2 applied the new Ctrl-without-Alt check to the whole drag-blocking condition, including its two arrow keys. §2.1.3 forbade changing the Ctrl+Arrow branch, so the key now falls through to that branch and moves the marker.
- Real `Control+Alt+Arrow`, `Meta+Alt+Arrow` and dispatched Ctrl+Alt+AltGraph during a drag also changed: they used to be blocked with the message and now do nothing silently. I rated that Info only.
- I could not produce the AltGraph-without-Alt state with real Playwright input on this Linux Chromium; it reported AltGraph as off. It is the state the task's own AG6 test uses, but no real platform has been shown to send it. I kept the reviewer's Medium rating; B may change it when ruling.

**Rows that passed:**
- **Scope and claims:** only the 3 granted files changed; the diff is 1 added line plus 11 substitutions, and the test file is add-only. Claims K1–K16 all match when re-run.
- **Tests:** the 13 targeted test files pass 231/231, and all 9 mutants turned their named rows red. The unmutated copy passed 25/25.
- **Browser:**
  - AltGr, Ctrl+Alt and Meta+Alt letter chords change nothing.
  - Plain Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z, Ctrl+E, Ctrl+L and Ctrl+Alt+O work as listed in the task.
  - Focus stays on the library option.
  - Doc 199 meets its checks. Its status line says "Completed (C round 267 PASS)", which is not true while the round is FAIL.
  - Pages showed 0 errors.
- **Auth:** an anonymous visitor gets the demo on `/studio-lab`. `/studio/middle-east` shows "Sign in required" and loads no audio. `/api/studio-token` returns 401 with no header, and 500 with no token for a fake Bearer. Premium access is not bypassed.
- **Not checked by me:** the full test suite, build, `npm run verify` and the smoke tests are left to the root gate. I did not re-run an export, because this change only touches the keyboard handler.

**For B:**
- Choose fix (a) or (b) for the STOP, and decide what the arrow keys should do during a drag before re-dispatching; A proposed test row AG7 for this.
- The task never listed drag plus Ctrl+Arrow as at risk, and B's pre-check had no drag case.
- Outside a drag, the same AltGraph chord also moves the marker. I measured that on the new code only; the branch is unchanged, so I assume the published code behaves the same, but I did not measure it there.

My files don't change any source; `store/` still shows only A's 3 changed files.

Files are in `tmp/studio-real-loop/`:
- c-round-267.md
- c-round-267.json
- c-round-267/
